description: A scene that prints an answer and quits is start, then wait. A start says under runtime whether runtime_* can reach the game. A start ends the run of its project and user:// folder, and goes beside any other. start and check first import what changed on disk since its import. Operations: start (needs projectPath): run the project until it quits or is stopped; stop: end the run and answer with the errors and warnings it printed; check (needs projectPath): boot headless, quit after a few frames, and report whether it booted clean; wait: wait for the run to end, stop in its debugger or crash, then answer as editor_output does; profile: where the run spends its time, by GDScript function. Default start.

andChildren.description: Also end what the game started for itself, such as workers. For op stop.

args.description: The game's own arguments, such as ["--level=2"]. For ops start, check.

callersOf.description: Also answer where scripts name this function: its name, or Class.name. For op profile.

engineArgs.description: Engine flags, such as ["--verbose"] or ["--max-fps", "60"]. --fixed-fps lets a headless game run faster than the clock. For ops start, check.

engineCalls.description: With profile: also time engine calls. Crashes a threaded game. For op start.

env.description: Environment variables for this run, a map of strings. For ops start, check.

executable.description: An exported build to run instead of the project, inside the project or absolute. No scene or profile. For op start.

frames.description: Frames to run before quitting. Default 3. For op check.

godot.description: An absolute path to another Godot for this run. For ops start, check.

graceful.description: Ask the game to close first. Default true. false ends it at once. For ops start, stop.

headless.description: true runs with no window, false forces one. Default a window where there is a display. For op start.

limit.description: Functions to answer with, most self time first. Default 30. For op profile.

mark.description: Set the run's mark at these totals, for a later profile with since "mark". For op profile.

pid.description: Its pid. A stop also takes a game of this project that no server keeps, as editor_status lists under runtimes. Not for ops start, check.

profile.description: Time the run's GDScript from its start, for op profile to read. Needs an engine built with debugging. For op start.

projectPath.description: Absolute project path. stop, wait, profile: optional, the project whose run is meant.

runtimeWaitMs.description: How long to wait for the game to announce its runtime. Default half as long again as the slowest of that scene's last five boots, from 5000 to 60000. 0 does not wait. For op start.

savesIn.description: An absolute directory to hold this run's user://, whose path runtime.userDir answers. macOS ignores it, so the run writes the player's own saves. For ops start, check.

scene.description: A scene to run instead of the main scene. A script is no scene: put it on a scene's root. For ops start, check.

silent.description: Default true: this server starts a windowed game muted. false lets a connected editor play it. A headless run is silent already, and the editor plays one only when the project's main_run_args hold --headless. args, engineArgs, env, savesIn, godot or executable make this server start it either way. debug_* cannot reach an executable. For op start.

since.description: Answer only what ran after the mark. For op profile.

suites.description: gdUnit4 suites to play instead of a scene: a suite file or test directory, or a list. Needs gdUnit4 and this release's tests addon in the project. For op start.

timeoutMs.description: check: how long before the boot is called hung, default 60000. wait: default 600000. For ops check, wait.

visible.description: Show the window on the desktop in use. By default on Windows it goes on a desktop of its own, with --disable-vsync and --max-fps 60. On Linux and macOS the window shows either way. For op start.

name: editor_run
title: Run the game
